originalTitle: Australia news live: Ben Carroll grilled about involvement in Victorian leadership spill
content: NSW government accepts all recommendations from inquest after Bondi Junction stabbing attack The NSW government has formally accepted all recommendations from a coronial inquest into the stabbing deaths of six people at Bondi Junction shopping centre in 2024. The final report into the attack made 13 recommendations directed to the government, 11 of which it will accept in full and two in principle. They include a new health-led response model for mental heath emergencies funded with $270m over the next 10 years and stronger community mental health services, among others. “The Government’s response outlines the significant work already underway across agencies to strengthen mental health care, enhance emergency preparedness and response, improve community safety, and deliver on the Coroner’s recommendations,” a press release reads. NSW health minister Ryan Park said in a statement: The Government’s response continues our work to strengthen mental health services, improve access to care and ensure people with severe and complex mental illness receive the support they need earlier and closer to home. We are investing in reforms that improve coordination across the health system and help people access the right care at the right time. Read more: Brother of former premier Perrottet to appear before NSW Icac The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption’s (Icac) Operation Rosny hearings resumed this morning. Today’s witness is Reformers member Jean-Claude Perrottet, the younger brother of former Liberal premier Dominic Perrottet. Icac is investigating whether Liberal figures including Jean-Claude solicited or accepted illegal donations for the recruitment or renewal of members to the Liberal party, a practice known as branch stacking, which is not itself illegal. Icac is investigating another allegation that Liberal figures including his brother, Charles Perrottet, solicited or accepted donations from fugitive property developer Jean Nassif in exchange for the pursuit of outcomes sought by Nassif. The inquiry has heard that Jean-Claude and Charles avoided being served summons to appear at a parliamentary inquiry which preceded Icac’s probe. Yesterday’s witness, NSW shadow attorney general, Damien Tudehope, who admitted to leaking a confidential draft report from the parliamentary inquiry to another Reformer, claimed to have discussed with Dominic Perrottet that Jean-Claude was in Fiji during the 2023 inquiry. Dominic Perrottet is not accused of any wrongdoing, while Jean-Claude and Charles have previously denied any wrongdoing. Victorian premier will read report from corruption watchdog ‘carefully’ Ben Carroll held a press conference after the release of the report by Victoria’s anti-corruption watchdog into the former Andrews government’s dealings with United Firefighters Union and its secretary Peter Marshall. The Victorian premier said he would “read the report carefully” and give “Victorians the action and the answers they deserve”. Carroll went on: This is poor behaviour. It is intolerable. I will take action. I will accept the recommendations and get on with implementing [them]. Victoria’s anti-corruption watchdog has tabled a long-awaited report into the former Daniel Andrews government’s dealings with the United Firefighters Union and its secretary Peter Marshall. The Operation Richmond report did not find that any individuals engaged in corrupt conduct, but it found that senior members of the Andrews government engaged in “serious and concerning” conduct in their dealings with Marshall when negotiating pay deals for the Country Fire Authority and Metropolitan Fire Brigade, and their later amalgamation into Fire Services Victoria. This included “actions contrary to policy, procedure and codes of conduct, deliberate attempts to conceal and mislead, and the misuse of information.” The Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission (Ibac) found the government made an “undisclosed deal” with Marshall, “to the exclusion of other key stakeholders,” which allowed him to “exert extraordinary influence over the negotiations” for both the CFA and MFB enterprise bargaining agreements. Ibac also found that Marshall was granted “privileged access” to responsible ministers. The final release of the findings comes after years of legal attempts by the UFU to keep the report secret, including a high court challenge. The investigation first began in 2018 following a tip-off that Marshall “blackmailed or otherwise compromised” Andrews “to change his position on the CFA EBA”. Ibac found no evidence of blackmail and did not substantiate the allegation, which both Andrews and Marshall denied. Victorian premier says he wants Suburban Rail Loop to be ‘most cost effective it can be’ On the Suburban Rail Loop, Carroll says he’s not going to be “ripping up contracts” but wants to ensure the project is “the most cost effective it can be”. So far the state has signed about $14.5bn worth of contracts for SRL East – a 26km stretch of tunnels between Cheltenham and Box Hill – with tunnelling to begin soon. Carroll said: This project is proceeding, but I want it done in a cost-effective, transparent way, making sure Victorians know that every dollar we spend on their behalf is treated with respect. Host Raf Epstein asked: “Does cost-effective mean you’ll spend less each year? Are you going to slow down spending on the SRL?” Carroll: “Raf, I’ve got no announcements to make on that today except to say this is a project for the state, just like Airport Rail, just like Melton electrification. I want a more integrated approach to Victoria’s transport system.” Epstein: “That sounds like you are going to slow down that project so you can spend some of those dollars elsewhere.” Carroll: “Raf, I am focused on a statewide integrated public transport system. chineseContent: 新南威尔士州政府接受 Bondi Junction 刺伤事件后调查的所有建议 新南威尔士州政府已正式接受对 2024 年 Bondi Junction 购物中心 6 人刺死事件进行的死因调查的所有建议。袭击事件的最终报告向政府提出了 13 项建议，其中 11 项将全部接受，2 项原则上接受。其中包括未来 10 年内拨款 2.7 亿美元的新的以健康为主导的精神卫生紧急响应模式，以及更强大的社区精神卫生服务等。一份新闻稿称：“政府的回应概述了各机构已经开展的重要工作，以加强精神卫生保健、加强应急准备和响应、改善社区安全以及落实验尸官的建议。”新南威尔士州卫生部长瑞安·帕克（Ryan Park）在一份声明中表示：政府的应对措施将继续我们的工作，以加强精神卫生服务，改善获得护理的机会，并确保患有严重和复杂精神疾病的人更早、离家更近地获得他们所需的支持。我们正在投资改革，以改善整个卫生系统的协调并帮助人们在正确的时间获得正确的护理。阅读更多：前总理佩罗特的兄弟将出席新南威尔士州反腐败独立委员会 (Icac) 的罗斯尼行动听证会今天上午恢复。今天的证人是改革党成员让-克洛德·佩罗泰 (Jean-Claude Perrottet)，他是前自由党总理多米尼克·佩罗泰 (Dominic Perrottet) 的弟弟。廉政公署正在调查包括让-克洛德在内的自由党人士是否为自由党招募或更新党员而索取或接受非法捐款，这种做法被称为“分支堆叠”，其本身并不违法。伊卡克是
